incidents.title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
incidents.summary:
A South Florida immigration attorney, Angel Leal, who has practiced law for over 30 years, reported that criminals are using artificial intelligence to impersonate him and defraud immigrants. Scammers created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos featuring Leal offering fraudulent immigration services. In the videos, the digital version of Leal promises US residency assistance to undocumented immigrants for $2,200. Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office, though suspicious activity first appeared in October. The fraud has escalated dramatically over the past three months.

Leal's office hired an anti-piracy company that removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The scams typically start with social media videos directing viewers to contact a WhatsApp number, then involve exchanging phony contracts and requesting payment through Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App. Leal warned immigrants to verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online and to be suspicious of immediate payment requests. He changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the fraud.

incidents.title: ASIC warns scammers are using AI to spin vast webs of deception
incidents.summary:
A fake news article featuring Reserve Bank Governor Michele Bullock in a heated interview with ABC finance presenter Alan Kohler has become the latest example of an emerging scam trend. The fabricated piece promoted Boulder Sparhaven, an unlicensed cryptocurrency trading platform, by creating a fictional confrontation. This incident demonstrates how scammers are increasingly using artificial intelligence to generate convincing deepfake content targeting well-known Australians, particularly Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Alan Kohler, and wealthy businesspeople like Gina Rinehart.

The Australian Securities and Investments Commission reports that AI-generated investment scams are rising rapidly and becoming more sophisticated. Last year, ASIC removed 19,400 scams total, including 7,051 fake investment platforms and 5,476 phishing attempts, representing significant increases from previous years. Scammers build elaborate webs of deception using fake news articles, reviews, and advertisements to lure victims. ASIC advises consumers to verify Australian Financial Services licence numbers through official registers before investing and warns that polished content and familiar branding do not guarantee legitimacy.

incidents.title: Sleep Staging Is Not Guesswork
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Oura, a smart ring manufacturer valued at $11 billion, faces a proposed class-action lawsuit filed by Clarkson Law Firm in San Francisco. The suit alleges that the company falsely advertised its sleep-tracking capabilities, claiming that Oura rings priced at $300 and up can accurately detect different sleep stages comparable to hospital sleep labs. The lawsuit contends that Oura's algorithms and sensors cannot measure the physiological signals needed for accurate sleep stage detection and instead rely on "AI-generated guesses" no better than random chance.

Oura disputes the allegations, stating that it stands behind its scientific research and accuracy claims. The company maintains that its rings use multiple physiological signals including heart rate and temperature patterns to estimate sleep stages, and that independent studies have validated these measurements against clinical polysomnography standards. The lawsuit seeks class-action status and a jury trial, though it remains unclear what compensation buyers might receive if the case proceeds or settles. This is not Oura's first legal challenge, as another ongoing class action alleges the company collected personal information without customer consent.

incidents.title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team discovered that Aurora ransomware, active since April 2026, has developed a Linux variant targeting ESXi environments and is abusing an AI tool called Cursor Agent to conduct exploitation attacks. Between April 8 and May 21, 2026, Aurora operators used Cursor Agent running Claude Sonnet to assist with hands-on exploitation across ten target organizations. The ransomware uses ChaCha20 encryption with RSA-4096 key wrapping and includes an ESXi mode that kills virtual machines, encrypts their files, and leaves ransom notes accessible via SSH banner.

The attackers also deployed custom tools including esxi_finder.py to scan networks for ESXi hypervisors and vCenter servers. A second cluster of Aurora activity was identified with medium confidence, affecting eight victim organizations across multiple countries including Israel, Germany, Austria, Spain, the United States, and Argentina. This second group used different tactics involving SQL Server exploitation, privilege escalation, and data exfiltration to self-hosted S3 storage. Gambit Security published indicators of compromise including IP addresses, domains, and file hashes to help organizations identify Aurora's infrastructure.

incidents.title: A Pizza Hut franchisee is suing over a forced AI system it says wrecked deliveries
incidents.summary:
A major Pizza Hut franchisee filed a lawsuit on May 6 in Texas alleging that Pizza Hut's new AI-powered delivery system, called Dragontail, caused operational failures and cost the company over $100 million in damages. Chaac Pizza Northeast, which operates approximately 111 Pizza Hut locations across the Northeast, claims the system gave DoorDash drivers real-time visibility into kitchen operations, causing drivers to wait up to fifteen minutes to batch multiple orders together rather than delivering pizzas immediately. This delay resulted in cold deliveries, customer dissatisfaction, and sharply declining sales across the franchisee's markets, including a swing from positive 10.19% to negative 9.78% year-over-year growth in New York City.

The lawsuit argues that Pizza Hut failed to adequately train operators on the system, ignored requests for support, and breached its franchise agreement by mandating the software without exercising proper business judgment. Before Dragontail's rollout in 2024, Chaac reported over 90 percent of deliveries arrived within thirty minutes and consistently exceeded system averages for customer satisfaction. Chaac is seeking more than $100 million in damages plus attorneys' fees. Pizza Hut said it would respond through legal channels but declined further comment at this time.

incidents.title: Inside the Fake Celebrity Podcast Scam Fooling Hollywood
incidents.summary:
Scammers are impersonating Terry Gross and other "Fresh Air" staff members to defraud aspiring guests. Authors, entertainers and public figures have received personalized emails claiming to offer interview opportunities, complete with details about their work and proposed topics. The messages eventually request payment, typically $250, for supposed production costs. A Misericordia University history professor and a comedy writer were among those targeted. WHYY, NPR and law enforcement are investigating the scheme.

According to cybersecurity experts, artificial intelligence has made impersonation scams more convincing and personalized than traditional mass-produced fraud attempts. Red flags include requests for payment, emails from unofficial addresses like "terrygrossfreshair@gmail.com," and a host personally handling logistics rather than production assistants. WHYY emphasized it never charges guests for interviews. Experts recommend verifying requests through legitimate organizational contacts and recognizing that high-profile individuals may reasonably receive interview invitations, which scammers exploit by targeting their vanity.

incidents.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda
incidents.summary:
# Summary

A fake American think tank called the Hanover Institute for Public Policy, funded by the Israeli government, published over 560,000 words across 124 reports in nine days using a platform designed to influence artificial intelligence chatbots. The reports presented pro-Israel arguments on contentious topics including genocide allegations, war crimes, and Palestinian starvation, all formatted like academic research with citations to legitimate sources. The New York media company Piro Inc registered the site with the U.S. Justice Department as Israeli government material, revealing an effort costing tens of millions of dollars to manipulate how AI systems frame Israeli policy arguments.

The broader campaign involved multiple contractors paid through European advertising group Havas Media, with Clock Tower X receiving $15 million and other firms receiving millions more. Israeli officials have expressed doubt about the campaign's effectiveness, with some calling it a waste of money as American public opinion has shifted significantly against Israel. Research shows 60 percent of Americans now view Israel unfavorably, up from 40 percent in 2022, and 31 percent believe Israeli military actions constitute genocide, suggesting that technical manipulation of AI systems cannot overcome public concern about actual policies.

incidents.title: Round Hill is suing Suno and Anthropic for up to $1B apiece. It isn’t looking to settle.
incidents.summary:
Major record labels including Universal Music Group, Sony Music, Warner Music, Capitol Records, and Atlantic Records have filed lawsuits against Udio and Suno, two popular AI music generators. The labels accuse both companies of illegally scraping massive amounts of copyrighted music without permission to train their artificial intelligence models, then using that training data to generate new songs that directly reproduce sections of famous recordings. The record labels submitted extensive documentation including a thumb drive of AI-generated examples that allegedly replicate copyrighted works from artists like The Beatles, Frank Sinatra, Michael Jackson, and others.

To support their claims, the record labels tested both AI music generators by inputting specific prompts describing popular songs, such as decade, genre, and artist style. They report successfully recreating versions of famous tracks multiple times, including songs by Chuck Berry and Mariah Carey. The lawsuits claim the companies have refused to disclose which songs were used for training data but previously argued their use constituted fair use. Udio was sued in New York while Suno was sued in Massachusetts, setting up a major legal battle over how generative AI services handle copyrighted material.

incidents.title: Sony Music moves to add more than 30,000 copyrighted recordings to its lawsuit against Udio
incidents.summary:
Universal Music Group has resolved its lawsuit against AI music startup Udio by reaching licensing agreements with the company. UMG had accused Udio of using copyrighted songs, including The Temptations' "My Girl," to train its artificial intelligence system that generates original music from text descriptions. Under the settlement terms, Udio will launch a new platform next year that only uses authorized and licensed music. The financial details of the agreement were not disclosed, but UMG's leadership stated the deal reflects their commitment to supporting artists while embracing new technologies.

Udio, founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind employees, has agreed to compensate artists who opt into the new platform, though specific details remain undisclosed. This marks Udio's first major licensing agreement with a record label. Udio has been used by millions of people since launching and has received backing from notable investors including musician will.i.am and venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz. Additionally, UMG announced a separate partnership with Stability AI to develop music creation tools for artists and producers.

incidents.title: AI Hallucinations in State Farm Insurance Outside Lawyers' Filings
incidents.summary:
# Summary

State Farm's lawyers apologized after their legal filings in a Los Angeles lawsuit contained artificial intelligence-generated fake cases, nonexistent quotes, and false legal holdings. The plaintiff, Fa'alagilagi Meni-Siliga, filed suit in July 2024 against State Farm and others after a 2020 house fire in Carson left her home uninhabitable. Following water damage during repairs, she alleged State Farm delayed approving necessary work, ultimately losing her home to foreclosure and draining her family's savings and retirement accounts. Attorney Jacquelene Robinson admitted using an AI tool called Irys to help prepare motions, believing it would check citations, and confirmed seven case citations across eight filings did not actually exist.

The case highlights growing concerns about AI use in the legal profession, with 41 percent of law firms and 47 percent of corporate legal departments now using generative AI. A worldwide database documents 1,922 legal hallucination cases, mostly in the United States. State Farm stated it expects external counsel to meet high ethical standards and confirm accuracy of filings. The trial is scheduled for October, and the firm has updated its AI policy, though specifics were not disclosed.

stories.Headline: Roundup: Chinese AI gaining popularity in Kenya for affordability, performance, customization
stories.Summary:
Chinese artificial intelligence models are becoming increasingly popular among Kenyan developers and technology companies due to their affordability, strong performance, and customizable open-source design. According to recent data, Chinese AI models represented roughly half of AI use on OpenRouter, up from less than 25 percent a year prior, and accounted for 19 of the 25 most-downloaded open-source systems on Hugging Face. Kenyan companies are adopting Chinese models like DeepSeek and Qwen for applications including legal technology, business intelligence, and document processing.

Local technology leaders highlight that Chinese models consume fewer computing resources than Western alternatives while delivering comparable or superior performance, making them practical for Kenya's limited GPU supply. The open-weight nature of these models allows developers to customize them for local languages and African-specific needs without building systems from scratch. Companies like JibuDocs and Qhala are already leveraging these models for innovative applications, while experts suggest potential uses in healthcare diagnostics and disaster prevention could serve underserved African communities.

stories.Summary:
Taiwan's government plans to invest over 40 billion Taiwan dollars, approximately 1.26 billion US dollars, to develop 10 major artificial intelligence projects next year. President William Lai has set an ambitious goal to train at least 500,000 AI professionals by 2040. The administration launched the AI Talent Ark Project this year to nurture talent through fundamental education, professional development, and data-driven approaches, aiming to build a large AI talent pool and strengthen Taiwan's competitiveness in technology sectors.

The government is also prioritizing technological sovereignty and national resilience. The Minister of Digital Affairs announced plans to accumulate at least 10,000 graphics processing units through private investment in AI computing centers within a year. Taiwan is focusing on developing sovereign AI systems that understand Taiwanese perspectives and languages, along with low-Earth-orbit satellite communications to ensure independent communication capabilities. Officials emphasized that technological sovereignty means focusing on critical technologies rather than developing every technology domestically.

stories.Headline: What We Know About Haryana Police's AI Task Force.
stories.Summary:
Haryana Police is establishing an Artificial Intelligence Task Force to expand AI use in law enforcement operations. An Indian Police Service officer will lead the initiative, which focuses on cybercrime investigations, financial transaction analysis, complaint management and court information processing. The police emphasized that AI will support human investigators rather than replace them, with officers responsible for verifying leads and making final decisions.

The task force will build on existing technology systems Haryana Police already uses, including a 2022 facial recognition program that deactivated nearly 1,000 fraudulent SIM cards and current cybercrime helplines. The police plan to implement safeguards around accuracy, transparency, data security and human oversight, though specific implementation details remain unclear. Haryana Police has not disclosed how it will test systems, measure errors, conduct audits or handle incorrect results, and has not explained how new AI capabilities will integrate with current infrastructure or whether it plans to use facial recognition or predictive policing technologies.

stories.Headline: Who Writes AI's Rules When Someone Else Owns the Machines?
stories.Summary:
# Summary

South Africa withdrew its Draft National AI Policy in April 2026 after discovering that at least six of its 67 academic references were fabricated, highlighting a broader challenge facing the Global South. The incident underscores a critical debate about who controls artificial intelligence governance and infrastructure. Currently, the United States and China host roughly 86% of global data centre capacity, giving them power to set rules and prices for AI systems worldwide. This concentration of computing power represents what critics call "tech colonialism," where developing nations provide data and demand but lack ownership and control over the technology itself.

BRICS countries and other Global South nations are attempting to shift AI governance away from Western-led standards by emphasizing digital sovereignty and development rights. They are seeking to anchor AI governance within the United Nations rather than OECD-led bodies and have established organizations like the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organisation. However, meaningful sovereignty requires owning physical infrastructure, not just adopting policies. The article notes that until developing nations build regional computing capacity and chip manufacturing capabilities, they remain dependent on foreign platforms controlled by American hyperscalers or Chinese firms. True sovereignty means choosing dependencies rather than having them imposed.

stories.Headline: EU places ChatGPT, Reddit, Roblox under strictest platform rules
stories.Summary:
The European Union has classified ChatGPT as a Very Large Online Search Engine and designated Reddit and Roblox as Very Large Online Platforms under its Digital Services Act. These three American companies will now face direct supervision from the European Commission and must comply with stricter requirements designed to address risks related to children, election integrity, and public security. The rules apply to services with over 45 million users in the EU, bringing the total number of regulated platforms to 28.

Companies failing to meet the new requirements within four months face fines up to 6 percent of their annual global revenue. Reddit reported 57.2 million EU users in July, while Roblox has 46.6 million. OpenAI stated it would prepare to meet ChatGPT's additional obligations, and Roblox welcomed the designation, emphasizing safety's importance. This designation adds another regulatory layer for ChatGPT, which already complies with the EU's Artificial Intelligence Act.

stories.Headline: CSA's Top Cloud Threats: Identity, AI -- Campus Technology
stories.Summary:
The Cloud Security Alliance surveyed 507 security professionals to identify the top threats to cloud computing in 2026. Identity and access management issues rose to the number one concern, moving up from second place in 2024, while misconfiguration dropped to fifth. Two artificial intelligence-related threats appeared in the rankings for the first time, including AI-enhanced attacks and AI system compromise. The top eleven threats also include insecure third-party resources, insecure APIs, advanced persistent threats, and inadequate cloud security strategy and governance.

The survey results reveal a significant shift in the cloud threat landscape, with organizations now prioritizing identity protection, artificial intelligence risks, and software supply chains over infrastructure-focused concerns. Security scores ranged closely from 7.95 for identity and access management to 7.45 for system vulnerabilities. The report aims to help organizations make informed risk-management decisions about cloud adoption by providing expert analysis of technical and business impacts, real-world examples, and corresponding security controls across cloud and AI environments.

stories.Headline: AIM Summit 2026 to Bring 50+ CMOs and 600+ Marketing Leaders Together for India's First Dedicated AI-in-Marketing Summit
stories.Summary:
India's first dedicated summit focused on artificial intelligence in marketing, called AIM Summit 2026, will convene over 50 chief marketing officers and 600+ marketing professionals. The event will take place September 17 in Bengaluru and September 18 in New Delhi, bringing together industry leaders from major brands including Paytm, Motorola, KFC, Nestle, and the Tata Group alongside AI innovators and technology companies. The summit aims to move beyond theoretical discussions about artificial intelligence toward practical, real-world applications and measurable business impact.

The summit will feature 50+ speakers, an AI Lab where attendees can experience technology firsthand, an AI Exhibition showcasing relevant tools, and awards recognizing marketing leaders leveraging artificial intelligence effectively. Organizers are curating the event in partnership with CXO Lanes, a community of over 500,000 chief executive officers across India. Sessions will focus on practical applications including content creation, personalization, customer experience, marketing automation and measurement, helping marketers understand how to implement AI strategies that demonstrate clear business value.

stories.Headline: AI Now Writes 86% of Paisabazaar's New Code, Reshaping How its Engineers Build Productively and Innovatively
stories.Summary:
Paisabazaar, India's leading financial products marketplace, reports that artificial intelligence now generates approximately 86 percent of new code written on its platform. The company's Chief Technology Officer emphasized that the objective is not to eliminate engineers but to enhance their productivity by automating repetitive tasks. This shift allows engineers to focus on architecture, problem-solving and innovation while accelerating development velocity and enabling teams to pursue a larger product roadmap.

The financial services company is expanding its engineering team despite increased AI involvement, demonstrating its commitment to using productivity gains for expansion rather than workforce reduction. AI-assisted development is integrated throughout the engineering lifecycle, including code writing, testing, debugging and documentation. The company plans to continue deepening AI adoption across both engineering and consumer-facing experiences to expand innovation, improve productivity and deliver more personalized financial services at scale.

stories.Headline: Dyna.Ai Selected as Technology Partner in Hong Kong's GenA.I. Sandbox++
stories.Summary:
Dyna.Ai, a Singapore-based AI company, has been selected as a technology partner in Hong Kong's new GenA.I. Sandbox++ program, marking its second consecutive selection by Hong Kong financial regulators. The sandbox was jointly launched by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, Securities and Futures Commission, Insurance Authority, and Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes Authority in collaboration with Cyberport. Out of nearly 100 regional proposals, 36 use cases involving 30 financial institutions and 27 technology providers were chosen, including major institutions like Bank of China (Hong Kong) and Manulife (International), alongside technology partners Google, IBM, and Dyna.Ai.

Unlike earlier programs focused on generative AI banking pilots, Sandbox++ expands across banking, insurance, securities, and pension funds to test Agentic AI systems that execute complex tasks under real-time governance. Dyna.Ai will demonstrate how financial institutions can safely delegate workflow execution to autonomous AI agents while maintaining strict oversight and compliance. The company plans to showcase its solutions and governance frameworks at LEAP 2026 in Riyadh later this year.

stories.Headline: Brazil archbishop establishes rules for use of AI in archdiocesan communications
stories.Summary:
Archbishop Josafá Menezes da Silva of Aracaju, Brazil has created guidelines for artificial intelligence use within his archdiocese. The rules require all AI-generated content to undergo human review before publication and to be clearly labeled to distinguish it from human-created work. The archbishop based these directives on Church teachings about human dignity and Pope Leo XIV's messages about AI's potential to create false realities and deepfakes.

The guidelines prohibit clergy from using AI to recreate their appearance, voice, or simulate statements they never made. However, AI can serve as an auxiliary tool for creating backgrounds, textures, illustrations, and assisting with visual composition. The archbishop emphasized that all Church communications must remain truthful and responsible, urging pastoral workers and the faithful to consult with church leadership when using technology to ensure it serves the Church's mission.
